fields.acceptance: go test ./internal/web/... and ./internal/daemon/... cover the default 7787, a changed port, off, and that the listen address is always 127.0.0.1, through the handler and the computed address with no socket bound; a test drives the listener manager through successive polls with rhiza.web.port 7787, then 8080, then off, then 7787 again, using a fake listener factory, and checks it starts, moves, stops and restarts the listener at each poll, and that --once and a set RHIZA_TEST_NOW open no listener. The daemon-settings testscript lists rhiza.web.port with its default, accepts rhiza daemon set rhiza.web.port 8080 and off, and rejects 0, 70000 and abc with an error naming the key.
fields.statement: The long-running daemon serves the web UI over HTTP on 127.0.0.1 at the port rhiza.web.port names, 7787 by default, and serves nothing when it is set to off; rhiza daemon --once never serves, and the daemon binds no listener when RHIZA_TEST_NOW is set, so the default test run binds no socket and parallel testscripts never race for the port. rhiza daemon set accepts rhiza.web.port only as a port number from 1 to 65535 or off, and a running daemon picks up a change at its next poll: it starts, moves or stops the listener to match.

fields.acceptance: The daemon-status testscript runs rhiza daemon --once, then rhiza daemon status shows http://127.0.0.1:7787 in text and --json; after rhiza daemon set rhiza.web.port off and another rhiza daemon --once, status shows the web UI off.
fields.statement: rhiza daemon status shows the web UI as the daemon's state file recorded it from the last poll's effective rhiza.web.port: its URL (http://127.0.0.1:<port>) for a port, or that the web UI is off; it reads the recorded setting and does not probe the listener.
